name: Inwall wallbounce: turned dashes from a cling step the dot up the wall
techNote: A wall (right face x 0, top y 600) over a floor, the finish box on its top. The start is a cling on its face at y 95 (the pauselift-wall lab's cling: stick toward the wall). Dash with the stick at rest (from a cling the dash flips away from the wall) and tilt toward the wall in the dash freeze (turnX -1): the turned dash faces the wall while wallJumpFacing still points away, so Movement.Update's step-up (806-816) lifts the dot in every rendered frame of the tick: 112 u (y 207), and it clings again. A second turned dash 3 inputs later lifts another 112 (y 318.8); the jump 2 inputs after it, clinging within the dash boost window, is the dash-into-wall wallbounce (Velocity (276, 730), momentum.y 400.8) from there: it peaks at y 705.8 and lands on the wall's top, finish on tick 38. `one-dash` (only the last turned dash and the jump) peaks at 536.8 and slides back down the face; `no-turn` (the main demo's inputs without the tilt) dashes away from the wall. Offline and turbo lift 112 a dash at the 280 fps clock (MacroEngine.FrameGrid, interpolation on).
